limitations: How well the land suits argentine black and white tegu, inside the range records place it. Habitat, not a count of animals and not a density.

The range is the places North Ground's published profile names as established populations ("Breeding populations in Florida (Hillsborough, Miami-Dade and Charlotte counties per FWC)"), drawn only where an openly licensed record confirms the species: Miami-Dade County, Florida (18 records). Records are too few to say more about where in or around those places it lives.
FWC also names breeding populations in Hillsborough and Charlotte counties, and NatureServe lists Georgia; no openly licensed record confirms them yet, so they are not drawn.

Records decide only whether ground is in the range; they never set a cell's colour, so where more people report wildlife does not become where there are more animals. Reptiles are recorded along roads, trails and in towns, and introduced species mostly where people report them; many occupied places have no record.
Unshaded ground is outside that range, rated unsuitable inside it, or open water, sea, ice or town the profile does not name as habitat. None of these is a finding that the species is absent.
Land cover is from 2019 and does not know forest age, recent fire or harvest.
Hunting geography and seasons play no part in this surface; the zone card says what is legal.

history.detail: First publication: range from clustered record squares, categorical habitat inside it.

Ground inside the range rated unsuitable kept as its own state; water, sea, ice and town masked for profiles that do not name them; values placed on the grid nodes the renderer samples (1.0.0 sat half a cell south-west); an island rule for sedentary families; elevation and coast requirements; confidence from components rather than record counts alone. The concentrated-population rule (2 counted squares holding 300 records) was set AFTER the first 2.0.0 build declined kalij pheasant on 15,421 records in three squares of Hawaii Island: the five-square minimum was meant to refuse a handful of scattered reports, and refused a real island population instead. Recorded as set after seeing the result.

Open water a profile names is drawn only within the profile's openWaterKm (else coastKm, else 5 km) of dry land, as the sea already was: under 2.0.0 mallard was painted across the middle of Lake Winnipeg. 'Water or wetland nearby' is a distance-weighted share falling to nothing at 20 km, replacing an unweighted 3 × 3 box that drew a hard-edged 0.3° square around every small lake (wild boar). Both set after seeing those surfaces. Gaps in the range no wider than the family's declared gapKm are joined by a morphological closing (grow by half the gap, shrink back), which can fill a hole between recorded places but never extend the range past its recorded edge or outside its convex hull; habitat and the masks still decide every joined cell. Set AFTER seeing the 2.0.0 alligator surface: 9,702 openly licensed records in 72 squares drew separate discs with central Florida blank — the records' sampling painted as absence. Recorded as set after seeing the result. For a family with an island rule, a population on a separate landmass needs that many records on it: set after kalij pheasant was drawn on Kauaʻi from 3 records, carried across the channel by the 150 km cluster rule. A cell is confirmed by 2 records in it and the eight cells around it, not in it alone: set after the 0.35° reads drew moose without the boreal core and red fox in fragments, because half of every species' record cells hold a single record, most with a record next door. And a correction, not a choice: each record square is now used at the size of the GBIF cell it stands for. The first reads' 0.35° squares were 1.40625° cells (GBIF aggregates 16 × 16 cells per map tile), so 2.0.0 drew ranges from a sixteenth of the ground the records covered, in bands with gaps between them.

methodologyStatedAs: Range: the established populations North Ground's published profile names, each drawn where an openly licensed record confirms it — Miami-Dade County, Florida — and ground within 20 km of those record cells; the ground between two named places is not joined. Habitat: each 0.1° cell's land cover read through this species' categorical profile, as for every range + habitat surface. No weight is fitted.
scaleStatedAs: Argentine black and white tegu: habitat opportunity. Colour is the habitat class for this species inside its range — red core, orange and yellow strong, green moderate, blue marginal. Habitat, not a count of animals.

season.warning: Habitat is read from the land, which does not change with the season; where the animals are within it can.

literature: Savannas and disturbed habitats such as forest clearings, roadsides and fence rows; tolerates flooded marshes. — North Ground's published profile of the species, citing Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, Argentine Black and White Tegu; NatureServe, NatureServe Explorer: Salvator merianae.
model.reading: Savanna and disturbed open ground are core, and so is forest beside open land (clearings, fence rows); farmland, town edges and marsh strong; closed forest moderate.
